description: We are a team of CIS NEDUET students
summary: FireLens (https://www.firelens.wiki) is an evidence-linked dashboard that turns NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) combustion archive into answers for fire safety in crewed spacecraft and habitats. Two decades of microgravity fire experiments, flown on the ISS and on uncrewed spacecraft, are spread across hundreds of PSI tables, reports and data files. FireLens harvests all 24 Combustion Science investigations into one validated snapshot: 2,009 source records and 2,632 report passages. An engineer picks a mission profile (ISS cabin, Moon base, pressurized rover, spacesuit) or sets oxygen, pressure and airflow, and FireLens ranks the experiments run closest to those conditions, maps which conditions have been tested and which have not, and compares investigations side by side. An AI assistant answers plain-language questions using only retrieved report excerpts and measurement rows. Every claim cites its accession, DOI, file and page or row, and when nothing is found the assistant says so. Code computes the numbers; the model only writes the words. Fire behaves differently without gravity, and future habitats will use cabin atmospheres unlike Earth's. FireLens shows designers what the existing evidence covers, and where it runs out.
details:
Source code: https://github.com/talhaadil48/firelens

WHAT IT DOES

FireLens answers one practical question for anyone designing a crewed habitat: which NASA experiments tell us the most about how fire will behave in the cabin we are designing?

- Explorer: choose a mission profile (Earth sea level, ISS cabin, Moon base, pressurized rover, spacesuit) or set oxygen fraction, pressure and airflow yourself. Investigations are ranked by how closely their measured test conditions match. A coverage map shows which combinations of conditions have been tested and where the gaps are.

- Investigation pages: purpose, hardware, test records, findings and publications for each experiment, always with its PSI accession, version and DOI.

- Compare: two or more investigations side by side, showing what is the same and what differs.

- Ask FireLens: plain-language questions answered with retrieval-augmented generation over report excerpts and measurement rows. Every claim is cited (accession, DOI, file, page or row), and any chart in an answer is drawn from the cited rows.

- Export: the records behind any view as CSV or JSON, with their sources attached.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Harvest: a Python pipeline pages through the public PSI catalogue, keeps Combustion Science investigations, and downloads each file manifest, the experimental CSV tables and the reports (Raw Data folders of up to 2 TB are linked, never copied).

2. Normalize: per-investigation YAML column maps convert units to one standard (oxygen fraction 0-1, pressure in kPa, flow in cm/s, sizes in mm). Pandera checks the schema, so bad rows are rejected instead of silently imported.

3. Snapshot: measurements go to Parquet, metadata to JSON, and report text is split into chunks for retrieval. The live snapshot covers 24 investigations, 22 experimental tables, 1,879 rankable measurements and 2,632 text passages.

4. Serve: a FastAPI service queries the snapshot with DuckDB. Rankings, ranges, counts and chart data are all computed in SQL. The language model only writes summaries and explanations from facts the API hands it.

5. Stay current: a nightly sync job checks PSI for changes, rebuilds and validates the snapshot, and publishes it. The API picks up the new snapshot within 15 minutes and never calls NASA while a user is browsing.

TRUSTWORTHINESS

- Numbers come from code, words from the model.

- Every claim cites a source. Missing values stay empty; nothing is invented to fill a gap.

- Each investigation is shown with its DOI, so results are traceable and reproducible.

- We state the limits plainly: mission profiles and ranking weights are design assumptions, not NASA specifications or fire-risk predictions. A gap on the coverage map means no evidence in this collection, not that no research exists. PSI has no partial-gravity combustion data, and FireLens does not make any up.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Without FireLens, an engineer, student or researcher has to search PSI by hand, open dozens of tables, reconcile units and read long reports. FireLens turns hours of archive work into minutes and shows the evidence behind every answer. It also shows clearly what has not been tested, which can help set priorities for future microgravity experiments. As crews prepare to live on the Moon and Mars, fire safety decisions should rest on data that can be traced to its source, and FireLens provides that trail.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES

- Languages: Python 3.12, TypeScript, SQL

- Data pipeline: HTTPX (async), pandas, Pandera, PyMuPDF, Beautiful Soup, Apache Arrow/Parquet

- Backend: FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pydantic, DuckDB

- Frontend: React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Plotly.js

- AI: OpenAI gpt-4o-mini via OpenRouter for summaries and cited answers; local deterministic embeddings for retrieval

- Cloud and DevOps: Microsoft Azure (Static Web Apps, Container Apps, Container Apps Jobs, Blob Storage, Application Insights), Docker, GitHub Actions and GitHub Container Registry. Deployments are gated on tests and a valid snapshot, smoke-tested, and rolled back automatically if they fail.

- Quality: pytest, Vitest, Ruff, typed API contracts shared between backend and frontend

- No hardware was required.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

FireLens does not just put a chatbot on top of NASA data. It splits the work between the code and the model: the code finds and calculates every figure, and the model only explains facts it has been given. The mission-profile ranking turns a scattered research archive into a design tool. The coverage map shows what is missing as clearly as what exists.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

- Scientific honesty: no invented values, clear scope limits, and an explicit "no evidence found" when retrieval finds nothing.

- Respect for NASA infrastructure: PSI is cached in snapshots, there are no live NASA calls in the request path, and multi-terabyte raw data is never downloaded.

- Units and comparability: conversions live in reviewed YAML maps, not hard-coded numbers.

- Reliability: validated snapshots, health checks and automatic rollback on the live deployment.

- Openness: the code is MIT licensed, the PSI data is CC0, and there is a full reference list plus an AI-usage disclosure in the repository.

- Scope: rockets and propellants are deliberately out of scope.
